A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LT-Soups study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, checklist, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled CIFAR100 experiments, benchmark evaluations of LT-Soups, and ablation, calibration, and computational results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark accuracy, TinyImageNet-LT analyses, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same progressive subsampling, full fine-tuning, EMA, bootstrapping, recursive weight averaging, and final classifier retraining. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same controlled CIFAR100 scenarios, CIFAR100-LT, Places-LT, ImageNet-LT, NIH-CXR-LT, and iNaturalist 2018, with TinyImageNet-LT used for ablations. No dataset, domain, or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments. Tables 15–18 rename PEFT to LIFT, retaining the same Shi et al. source, backbone, and scores; this does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: The controlled imbalance sweep, class-frequency groups, accuracy metrics, CLIP ViT-B/16 backbone, validation-based selection, training settings, and calibration temperature tuning are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix A retain the same subsampling, classifier retraining, component, merging, loss, calibration, PEFT compatibility, and hyperparameter analyses, with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 is identical: experiments use a single random seed, except for multiple seeds required within model soups, and no statistical uncertainty estimates are reported. No reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, and the plotted images are identical. For example, LT-Soups retains 83.5 overall accuracy on CIFAR100-LT in Table 1 and 1.36 ECE in Table 7.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the logit-adjustment loss, and the subsampling, recursive averaging, and EMA formulas retain the same mathematical content. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same head-tail-ratio motivation, two-stage LT-Soups contribution, and claims of robust performance across imbalance regimes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the PEFT head/tail trade-off, subsampling and averaging effects, and domain-dependent merging weights are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitation concerning the fixed-threshold head/tail division.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D retain the same optimizer, hyperparameters, scheduling, hardware/software, and training-cost disclosures. Dataset details, validation procedures, and the code-access link are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Full bibliography entries added for works such as DiVE, PaCo, and GML correspond to sources already cited in v1's appendix tables; they complete existing citations without expanding related-work coverage.

P1.justification: Author-year citations become numbered citations throughout, and missing full bibliography entries are supplied. Other edits include PEFT-to-LIFT labels in Tables 15–18 and minor punctuation; substantive prose and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Shorter citations alter table widths and scaling, notably in Tables 1–2 and 13–18. Text and float placement also shift, including Figure 3 moving before the Section 4 heading. Figures, captions, and table organization remain otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies missing full references for already cited baselines and improves the legibility of crowded comparison tables through compact citations. These changes modestly improve source traceability and presentation. The methods, empirical evidence, and uncertainty-reporting limitations remain unchanged.
